focusDirective: the released runs' tail, the nested force-faults addition, remaining wasteful tails on the merged tree

hypothesis.title: A second stall clock marked only by plan-level progress, learned from the same probes, ends active runs whose plan has stopped advancing
hypothesis.description: stall_cap.rs gains a second RunClock per run whose marks are only (a) history rows other than timer firings and (d) plan releases; acted deliveries and acted timers (marks b and c) do not re-arm it. It is learned exactly as the existing clock is: every completed run-cap probe reports its longest plan-quiet gap into a second ScopeAccum table keyed by the configured budget, same QUANTILE 0.99, HEADROOM 1.5, MIN_COMPLETED_SAMPLES 200 and doubling checkpoints, so no constant is added; probes are never cut, so both learners stay unbiased. exec_plan (path.rs) feeds both clocks each step with the same suspended flag; a run treated on the new bit ends at the first step where either clock exceeds its own cap, taking the existing stall exit (release cell runs release at that first stall exactly as now, of whichever clock fired). Treated: half of the stall cap's treated runs by a salt of its own (bit planProgressClock = 1<<28, the retired clientProgressRelease row in VARIANT_BITS renamed), crossing the release split so all four cells are readable. Counters added under stall_cap.plan_clock: stops (runs ended by the plan clock while the fine clock was under its cap), steps_saved_sum against the frozen run cap, probes_keyed, cap_max_scope, and per-cell runs/plan_complete/steps. No config field.
hypothesis.rationale: The merged stall clock counts a state write as progress, so a run whose nodes keep writing state while its plan never advances is never stalled and runs to the learned run cap (2,843 and 3,635 steps in the 6,000 scope, 1,500 in the short scope). On the fresh baseline these active cap-enders are the largest step sink left: termination.all.learned_cap_reached 152,451/125,808 plus iterations_exhausted 146,464/145,098 per chunk against stall_cap_reached 274,867/238,145 and plan_complete 216,437/197,410; prefix_extension.all.budget_releasing is 573,782 of 790,380 runs (runs that ended at a budget while still releasing runnables), steps_idle_sum is 31 and tail_without_release_sum 7,662, so the tails are active, not idle. On the grid cells pooled over both chunks the cut cell averages 1,438 steps per run against a stall cap of 827/791: the cap-enders inside it carry most of its steps. A run's plan-level progress (client invocation and response rows, fault rows, plan releases) is what a completing run must keep producing, so its longest plan-quiet gap in completing probes is a learned bound with the same justification as the merged cap; a run beyond 1.5x its p99 is one the protocol is not converging in. The per-step marks are already computed (stall_cap.marks.rows 9.35M, releases 6.2M per chunk), so the second clock is two integer updates per step. The release cell's residual runs (35,793/34,856 per chunk that end neither by completion nor second stall) are the same active tails and end earlier on the crossed cell, which is the directive's item (1) by a route the counters support.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Stated without any handler, message or role: a run is stalled when its plan has not advanced for longer than 1.5x the 99th percentile of the longest such gap among completing uncut runs of the same budget. The bound is learned per session from probes, so another protocol needs no value: a protocol whose requests take long to answer after faults learns a long plan-quiet cap, one that answers quickly learns a short one, and anyone can read the learned value off stall_cap.plan_clock.cap_max_scope and the over-cap completion counter, which is how the merged cap's fitness was read.

prediction.mechanism: Bit planProgressClock = 1<<28, salt of its own over the stall cap's treated runs, treated share 3/8 of all runs (half of the treated cell), probes exempt, crossing the release bit 1<<12. The effect is on run length: treated runs that would have run to the learned run cap end at the plan clock instead, so the internal rung reads steps per run treated over control on the treated cells at 0.75-0.90 with depth8 per run inside [0.97, 1.03] as the preservation guard (the merged cap read 1.00 on this guard: untreated 0.01868 against cut 0.01859 depth8 per run on the fresh baseline), and the gain is read cross-binary as depth8 events per explore-second through throughput: runs per second [1.08, 1.25], depth8 per second [1.06, 1.25]. Depth10 per run on the crossed release cell is expected at or above 1.0 because released runs' active residual tails end earlier without losing their release; cross-binary depth10 per second [1.05, 1.30]. Shared state: both learners are fed only by uncut probes, so the treated split changes neither learner; the effect is per run and readable internally, unlike a learner-delivered effect.
prediction.independentObservable: termination.all.learned_cap_reached + termination.all.iterations_exhausted per chunk falls to at most 0.75x the fresh baseline's (at most 225,000 on seed 1000 from 298,915; at most 205,000 on seed 1001 from 270,906) while stall_cap.plan_clock.cap_max_scope in the 6,000 scope reads below 0.8x run_cap.current_cap_max_scope (below 2,270 against 2,843 on seed 1000); stall_cap.plan_clock.probe_over_cap_completions stays at or below 2% of probes_keyed.
prediction.falsifier: The learned plan-quiet cap in the 6,000 scope reads at or above 0.9x the learned run cap on both seeds (the clock is inert and stops fall under the floor), or with the floor met depth8 per run treated over control reads below 0.97 or depth10 per run below 0.90 on the treated cells, or cross-binary depth8 per second reads at or below 1.00 pooled.
prediction.costClause: Cross-binary throughput at or above 1.05 (the mechanism removes steps; a reading below 1.00 refutes it outright).

hypothesis.redTeam: The plan-quiet p99 among completing probes may sit close to the learned run cap: a completing run can hold a client operation open across a whole view change, so the learned plan-quiet cap times 1.5 could read near 2,843 and cut almost nothing (the candidate's own inertness falsifier). Depth events on the oracle path occur after a restart row inside a plan-quiet segment; if a long plan-quiet segment precedes the depth event on some runs, the clock removes them and the depth8 per-run guard fails. On the crossed release cell the plan clock changes when the first release fires (whichever clock trips first), so the parent's release timing is altered on half its cell. The gain is throughput and reads cross-binary against a cache whose two seeds differ by 12 percent in runs per second, so a real 1.10 can read as noise on one seed pair.

The learned design is the merged cap's, so no constant is added; both learners are fed by uncut probes so the treated split moves no shared state and the internal preservation guard is valid. Run-length mechanism: graded cross-binary on depth8 per explore-second with the internal depth8 per-run guard, as the candidate states. Stands first in the stall family: it targets the largest remaining step sink (the active learned-cap and budget enders on every treated run, not only the post-release tail) and subsumes the post-release cap.

rejected.reason: Operator work on the merged form, not a hypothesis the loop can grade. It removes the stall cap's control cell (TREATED_PERIOD 4 -> 1): no treatment bit, no per-run off state, so the only read is cross-binary at an arithmetic 1.08x runs per second (verified: untreated 289,795 runs / 2,424 steps / 9,629 us against cut 435,168 / 1,438 / 6,757 and release 1,761 / 7,768; grid wall per run 7,854 -> 7,262 us) on a cache whose two seeds differ by 12 percent, and it discards the untreated row table and the bit-1024 per-cell read the panel and every future cap re-read rely on, leaving the cap's fitness on probes alone. Its per-run preservation premise is already answered by the fresh cache (depth8 0.01868 against 0.01859, depth10 0.000304 against 0.000319, exact), so nothing falsifiable is left to run; the direction review after iteration 77 already assigned the fold to the operator. One cited detail is false: timer-context probes read depth8 per run 0.0072, not 0.0037 (conclusion unchanged).

reviewSummary: Eleven kept, one rejected. Stall family: the plan-progress second clock stands first (7-0; every cited counter exact on the fresh merged cache; learned like the merged cap; run-length mechanism read cross-binary with an internal depth8 per-run guard), the repeated release second (6-0; rewritten to a cross-binary depth10 primary with the internal contrast as guard), the nested force-faults third (3-0; superseded as the nesting by the repeat, restart floor re-grounded to 12,000, crossing with the merged release cell stated), the post-release cap fourth (3-0; sub-floor payoff by its own arithmetic and subsumed by the plan clock). The untreated-quarter fold is rejected as operator merge-form work: no bit, control cell removed, per-cell read lost, its arithmetic verified (1.08x runs per second) and its premise already answered. Outside the family: crash hold in the restarted-peer window 5-0 (internal per-run read, predicate frequency unmeasured, census gate), replay parent by arm set 4-0 (fidelity base verified at 0.54/0.47, bits 1<<22/1<<23, description's 1<<12/1<<10 stale), run-local counters 5-2 (identities verified; hotspot unprofiled; seed swing limits the read), stalled parents 3-0 (guard re-based; the cut lands on the wedged state), PCT change points 3-0, headroom dose 2-0 (premise figures false again), cover-edge reversal 2-0. All claimed bits are retired rows unread in spur-core and mutually distinct; 1<<30 is positive in the i32 tag (Int32 column) and decide.ts uses a plain bitwise and, so no sign or probe collision. False or stale claims named: headroom dose's cap and cap-ender figures (2,183/3,275 and 295,328 against 2,843/3,635 and 152,451/125,808); the fold's timer-probe depth8 (0.0037 against 0.0072); withheld-faults' prior-cache counts (71,637 unrecovered crashes now 64,756; outstanding 4.0M now 3.4M); stalled-parents' prior-cache counts (352,842 stops now 274,867; guard 137,588/140,189 now 145,187/129,440); replay-arm's per-run bases (fresh 0.0083 now 0.0124).

otherCandidates.scoreReason: Direct continuation of the merged parent on the mechanism the loop has just measured (release over cut depth10 per run 0.000600 against 0.000319, 261 against 139 events, plan completion 0.391 against 0.164, all exact on the fresh cache); the once-only guard release_step.is_none() is real at path.rs exec_plan; second-stall stops 88,007/73,248 ground the firing floor; late responses 199 of 782,970 verified. Bit 1<<29 free. Keeps plan order and issues both operations and faults, which is why it stands above the force-faults nesting. Run-length mechanism: rewritten to read cross-binary on the depth10 advance rung with the internal contrast and depth8 per run as guards.
otherCandidates.redTeam: The parent's depth10 gain came from the first layer of the plan issued onto a quiet system; the second layer holds fewer faults (16.6k fault dependents over 186k releases is 0.09 per release) and is often the end of the plan, so repeats mostly re-issue client operations into the same wedge and lengthen runs by a full stall cap each. The parent already costs 4.5 percent throughput; each repeat adds about 800 quiet steps on 3/16 of runs, and released runs that keep issuing operations already run to the iteration budget. The internal contrast (treated half against the once-only half of the release cell) is unbalanced on run length, so the per-run depth10 ratio inherits the parent's known selection: longer runs hold more depth events. If the repeated releases end in a stall without fresh operations the mechanism is a no-op that still paid the second stall.

predictionRewrite.mechanism: Bit stallReleaseRepeat = 1<<29 under its own salt over half of the release cell (3/16 of non-probe runs; probes exempt). Treated runs release at every stall that finds a fresh in-progress operation; a stall with none ends the run as the parent does. The effect lengthens runs, so the primary read is cross-binary: depth10 events per explore-second against the fresh merged-tree cache in [1.10, 1.40] pooled over two chunks, refuted at or below 1.00 with the floor met. Guards: internal depth10 per run treated over the once-only half of the release cell at or above 1.00 (below 0.95 is a regression of the parent's gain); depth8 per run treated over control in [0.97, 1.05]; cross-binary depth8 per second at or above 0.95.

predictionRewrite.costClause: Cross-binary throughput at or above 0.95 of the fresh merged-tree cache.

otherCandidates.scoreReason: Mechanism-level alternative to the stall family with a clear per-run internal read: SendLedger carries entries_at_restart, in_flight and ghost_acted_since_restart (state.rs), crash_hold_mask sits at scheduler.rs:704, crash_phase::WINDOW is 96 and fault_timing::draw_hold and cap_reserve exist, and a hold is counted as suspended by the stall clock through crash_hold_until, so treated and untreated runs stay length-matched. otherCandidates.redTeam: The cited 73 percent (recoveries_with_own_prior_sends_inflight) measures a restarted node's pre-crash ghost sends, not post-restart sends, so the frequency of the predicate the hold waits for is unmeasured; with purgatory delay_probability 0.0 in general_vr.json nothing holds a fresh post-restart send back, so the window between a restart and the dispatch of its sends is a handful of network steps. A crash whose placement step arrives outside such a window waits up to 96 steps for another node to restart; with 1-3 crashes per run most holds will expire and the crash fires as stock, so landed_in_window/armed may fall under the 0.30 inapplicability line. The rung's event is the restarted node's own Recovery reaching a recovered peer before that peer sees the ghost StartViewChange; another node crashing during the restart window is adjacent to that shape, not the shape itself.

predictionRewrite.mechanism: Treatment bit replayArmMatched = 1<<22 on a quarter of prefix slots drawn by a salted phase of the run id; inverse bit replayArmMismatched = 1<<23 on another quarter; the stock half of prefix slots is the matched control (co-bits replaySlot, replayPrefix). Bits 1<<12 and 1<<10 are taken (stallRelease, stallCap) and must not be used. Per-run depth>=8 ratio of the matched quarter to the stock prefix half, probe-free, co-bit matched on the arm bits, in [1.03, 1.12], pooled over up to four chunks and reported as unresolved rather than confirmed if the interval straddles 1.03; the mismatched quarter in [0.86, 0.99]. The bits change which parent tape a slot receives, never how a run consumes or records one; parents are admitted only from fresh runs.
